item.title: [New] Storm-0940 used the ARTEX agentic framework and compromised ConnectWise multi-tenant apps to act app-only in customer tenants; one app self-assigned Global Administrator
item.description:
An app your tenant consented to years ago acted as the attacker with no user sign-in and no MFA prompt; the review window Microsoft asks for starts 1 October, so logs with shorter retention are already losing the evidence.

Threat Intel · Search every tenant by application ID, keep the ConnectWise apps disabled without deleting them, export service principal sign-ins, Graph activity and Entra audit from 1 October, and review credential additions, app-role assignments and role changes made by those service principals.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.description:
Every EWS application still in use, Apple Mail and Calendar on macOS and classic Outlook for Mac among them, either breaks now or survives on a temporary exception that re-opens the protocol Midnight Blizzard used; the exception expires on 1 April 2027 regardless.

Exchange Online · Pull the EWS usage report, list the apps by App ID, decide per app whether it gets a temporary entry in the EWS allowed App IDs list, and alert on any change to EwsEnabled or EwsAllowedAppIDs in the Exchange admin audit log.

item.title: [New] Entra ID Protection documents a new real-time risk detection, Suspicious credential addition (riskEventType suspiciousCredentialAddition), for an authentication method added under suspicious circumstances
item.description:
Registering a second authentication method is how an account takeover becomes persistent; a real-time risk on that step can drive a user-risk Conditional Access policy before the attacker's own method is used.

Entra · Add suspiciousCredentialAddition to the riskEventType lists your Sentinel and Defender rules match on, check that user-risk policies require remediation for it, and review the first detections against the AuditLogs 'User registered security info' events.

item.description:
Microsoft Teams will change voicemail email delivery by early March 2027, moving caller info from the email From field to the Subject line and allowing organizations to use their own domains for sending. Organizations should update mail-flow rules accordingly; no new compliance requirements arise.

item.description:
Microsoft is retiring the Copilot Studio app in Teams by February 2027, transitioning all chatbot agent creation and management to the Copilot Studio web app. Editing in Teams ends January 2027. Users and admins should switch to the web app and update related documentation accordingly.

item.title: [Message Center] MC1511052 Upcoming changes to Agents in SharePoint and OneDrive
item.description:
SharePoint and OneDrive agents using the .agent file format will be upgraded to integrate with Microsoft Copilot’s extensibility ecosystem. From mid-November 2026, new agents use the Copilot Agent Builder, with .agent files supported until March 2027, after which they stop working. Organizations should prepare to upgrade agents and adopt new management and governance tools.

item.title: [Message Center] MC1510951 Windows updates are available for 2026 time zone changes in Canada
item.description:
Windows updates are available to support 2026 time zone changes in Manitoba, Alberta, and British Columbia, effective November 1, 2026. Devices must install updates and select new region-specific time zones to avoid incorrect local time. Guidance for Outlook and interim steps are provided.
